newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica insurance firm sells bank stakes.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica insurance firm sells bank stakes.

text.p: Officials from Life of Jamaica, the country's largest insurance firm, said Friday the company was selling its stake in two local banks to the government in order to raise cash.

LOJ will sell its 30 percent stake in CIBC Jamaica, the local subsidiary of Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, and its 60 percent stake in CitizensBank, to the Financial Sector Adjustment Company (FINSAC), the agency set up to help the financial sector out of its current crisis.

Both banks are listed and traded on the Kingston exchange. The sale and a J$1.2 billion capital injection from FINSAC will net Life of Jamaica J$2 billion ($57.14 million), which it will use to pay down short-term debt.

Under the rules of the stock exchange, FINSAC must now make the same offer to other CitizensBank shareholders. These include Puerto Rico's BanPonce Corp, which last year acquired 20 percent of the bank. Citizens operates in Jamaica and Guyana, and has an agency in Miami.

LOJ's sale of its banking subsidiary was an alternative to the agency's acquisition of 25 percent of LOJ itself. Company officials say LOJ has been getting "positive signals" to efforts begun last year to raise J$1.5 billion ($42.85 million) in equity from overseas, but potential investors had said they would not invest if FINSAC were a shareholder.

A total of five insurance and financial services conglomerates have applied to FINSAC for assistance. The government intends to raise J$12.3 billion ($351.4 million) in medium term bonds, which it will use to acquire preference shares, plus 25 pct of the ordinary shares, in the companies involved.
The shares acquired by FINSAC will subsequently be sold on the market, rather than back to the companies, in order to broaden the equity and ownership base.
